tool_versions.klt_invocation: uvx --from "klayout-tools==0.9.1" klt -- the PIN_KLT release in scripts/setup-env.sh, which CI's signoff job also reads. The host's own klt dev build was not used.

command: scripts/synth-soc.sh (x2: unmodified main @ 2814179 in a detached scratch worktree, then this commit's tree); verification/tools/lint_rtl.sh (default and SRAM_MACRO_V forms, plus a temporary depth-dependent break that only the alternate-depth leg caught); make -C verification xbar periph boot soc soc-negative soc-gate; verification/tools/tests/test_lint_rtl.sh; the three signoff.yml legs via klt signoff --check
note: Resynthesis for issue #182 (leftovers from the ISRAM_1RW removal, #172): soc_fabric's per_gnt has been a driver with no reader since the *_gnt_i ports went, and because it kept its public RTL wire name Yosys retained a conb_1 tie-high whose only consumer was that wire. Deleting the signal and its constant assign is the whole RTL change; the same change regains a behavioural alternate-depth lint pass (ISRAM_AW=10 DSRAM_AW=10, no ISRAM_1RW), stops rtl/README.md presenting the depths as a knob, and rewrites obi_bench.py's grant paragraph to the fabric's post-#181 contract. synth_result.json is this commit's klt output; synth_result_baseline.json is the unmodified-main run's, kept so the before figures are auditable rather than asserted. The baseline netlist reproduced main's committed one byte-for-byte (sha256 e4592eca...), so the after-delta is this change, not the toolchain. Both runs used TMPDIR unset -- klt synthesize deadlocks in Yosys' abc pass on this host under the loom sandbox TMPDIR (same note as the records this one follows; filed at 2AMLogic/klayout-tools); every committed netlist was produced that way.

after.combinational_only: the entire delta is one conb_1 tie-high (7302 -> 7301); every other cell type, every flop count, all 8 SRAM macro instances and the soc_top port list are identical

supersedes.note: records/soc-sta-preroute/ and records/soc-pnr/ bind that netlist and so describe a netlist one change old. This change removes one dangling tie cell and is logic-identical otherwise (sequential_area_um2 identical at 70829.1808, every flop count identical), so no recorded timing claim moves in the unsafe direction -- but re-running pre-route STA and P&R on the current netlist is outstanding work, not covered here. The macro instance hierarchy (u_fabric/g_isram_1rw1r.u_isram/g_bank[N].u_macro, u_dsram/g_bank[N].u_macro) is unchanged, so flow/soc/pnr_request.json macro paths remain valid.
